/-!
# Conjecture 9.71

by A. N. Fomin

Is it true that every infinite 2-transitive permutation group with locally
soluble point stabilizer has a non-trivial irreducible finite-dimensional
representation over some field?

A permutation group on a set $\Omega$ is modelled as a group $G$ together with
a faithful action of $G$ on $\Omega$. A group is locally soluble if every
finitely generated subgroup is soluble. A representation is non-trivial if
some group element does not act as the identity.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.71» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Infinite G] (Ω : Type) [MulAction G Ω] [FaithfulSMul G Ω],
      IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2 →
      (∀ ω : Ω, IsLocallySolvable (stabilizer G ω)) →
      ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (V : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup V) (_ : Module K V)
        (_ : FiniteDimensional K V) (ρ : Representation K G V),
        ρ.IsIrreducible ∧ ¬ ρ.IsTrivial := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Is it true that every infinite 2-transitive permutation group with locally
soluble point stabilizer has a non-trivial irreducible finite-dimensional
representation over some field?

Here $G$ is an infinite group acting faithfully and 2-transitively on a set
$\Omega$ (which is then infinite as well), with all point stabilizers
$G_\omega$ locally soluble. Since $G$ is transitive on $\Omega$, the point
stabilizers are conjugate, so asking this for one point or for all points is
equivalent. The conclusion asks for a field $K$ of any characteristic, a
finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$ and a representation
$\rho \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}(V)$ that is irreducible (so $V \neq 0$ and $V$
has no $G$-invariant subspaces other than $0$ and $V$) and not the trivial
representation.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question, so the Prop is the universal statement itself (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G ...): G is an infinite group acting faithfully and 2-transitively on a set Ω (necessarily infinite since the action is faithful), the stabilizer G_α is locally soluble (all point stabilizers are conjugate, so one or all is equivalent), and the conclusion asserts existence of some field K (arbitrary characteristic) and a finite-dimensional K-vector space V with a G-action that is irreducible (nonzero, no proper nonzero G-invariant subspace) and non-trivial (some element acts non-identically).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates give mutually equivalent, faithful formalizations: G infinite, faithful MulAction on Ω (= permutation group), Mathlib's IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2 (checked via is_two_pretransitive_iff to be ordinary 2-transitivity; c05 spells it out inline equivalently), every point stabilizer locally soluble (standard definition: every finitely generated subgroup is soluble; ∀ points ⇔ one point since stabilizers are conjugate under transitivity), and conclusion ∃ field K (any characteristic), finite-dimensional V, ρ : Representation K G V with ρ.IsIrreducible (extends IsSimpleOrder on subrepresentations, so V ≠ 0 and no proper nonzero invariant subspace) ∧ non-trivial (¬ρ.IsTrivial, verified equivalent to ∃ g, ρ g ≠ LinearMap.id used by c01/c04/c05/c07). c08 chosen because it is the most complete and idiomatic: documented bespoke IsLocallySolvable using Subgroup.FG, an API lemma and a test as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for bespoke definitions, and clear docstrings. Only docstring wording was lightly edited; compiles with only the sorry warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.71

by A. N. Fomin

Is it true that every infinite 2-transitive permutation group with locally
soluble point stabilizer has a non-trivial irreducible finite-dimensional
representation over some field?

A permutation group on a set $\Omega$ is modelled as a group $G$ together with
a faithful action of $G$ on $\Omega$. A group is locally soluble if every
finitely generated subgroup is soluble. A representation is non-trivial if
some group element does not act as the identity.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open MulAction

namespace Kourovka.«9.71»

/-- A group is locally soluble if every finitely generated subgroup is soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

/-- Every soluble group is locally soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallySolvable.of_isSolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsSolvable G] :
    IsLocallySolvable G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- The trivial group is locally soluble. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallySolvable.unit : IsLocallySolvable Unit :=
  IsLocallySolvable.of_isSolvable Unit

/--
Is it true that every infinite 2-transitive permutation group with locally
soluble point stabilizer has a non-trivial irreducible finite-dimensional
representation over some field?

Here $G$ is an infinite group acting faithfully and 2-transitively on a set
$\Omega$ (which is then infinite as well), with all point stabilizers
$G_\omega$ locally soluble. Since $G$ is transitive on $\Omega$, the point
stabilizers are conjugate, so asking this for one point or for all points is
equivalent. The conclusion asks for a field $K$ of any characteristic, a
finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$ and a representation
$\rho \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}(V)$ that is irreducible (so $V \neq 0$ and $V$
has no $G$-invariant subspaces other than $0$ and $V$) and not the trivial
representation.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.71» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Infinite G] (Ω : Type) [MulAction G Ω] [FaithfulSMul G Ω],
      IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2 →
      (∀ ω : Ω, IsLocallySolvable (stabilizer G ω)) →
      ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (V : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup V) (_ : Module K V)
        (_ : FiniteDimensional K V) (ρ : Representation K G V),
        ρ.IsIrreducible ∧ ¬ ρ.IsTrivial := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.71»

items: 'Permutation group' is modelled as a group G with a faithful action on a type Ω ([MulAction G Ω] [FaithfulSMul G Ω]) rather than as a Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω); the two are equivalent.

'Infinite' is placed on G ([Infinite G]). Given faithfulness this is equivalent to Ω being infinite, and it excludes the degenerate |Ω| ≤ 1 case where 2-transitivity holds vacuously (there G would be trivial, hence not infinite).

'Locally soluble point stabilizer' is stated for all points ω (∀ ω, IsLocallySolvable (stabilizer G ω)). Ω is nonempty (else faithfulness forces G trivial) and 2-transitivity implies transitivity, so all stabilizers are conjugate and ∀ ω ⇔ ∃ ω.
'2-transitive' is Mathlib's MulAction.IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2, i.e. transitive on ordered pairs of distinct points (not sharply 2-transitive).

'Non-trivial' is read as 'not the trivial representation' (¬ ρ.IsTrivial, i.e. some g acts non-identically), not merely V ≠ 0; V ≠ 0 already follows from irreducibility, and every group has the trivial 1-dimensional irreducible representation, so this is the only meaningful reading. 'Irreducible' is Representation.IsIrreducible (IsSimpleOrder on subrepresentations).

The field K and space V are quantified in Type (universe 0), consistent with G : Type; this loses nothing since a finite-dimensional irreducible representation over any field restricts to the subfield generated by the matrix entries (of cardinality ≤ max(|G|, ℵ₀)) and remains irreducible.
Field K has arbitrary characteristic, as the statement says 'over some field'.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no candidate omitted it and no decomposition objections were raised. Modeling points a reviewer should be aware of: (1) 'Infinite' is placed on G; Ω is then automatically infinite because the action is faithful, and the degenerate |Ω| ≤ 1 case (where 2-transitivity is vacuous) is excluded because faithfulness would force G trivial. (2) K, V are quantified in Type (universe 0) alongside G : Type, following repository convention; this loses nothing since a finite-dimensional irreducible non-trivial representation can be realised over the subfield generated by the matrix entries. (3) 'Non-trivial' is read as 'not the trivial representation' (some g acts non-identically), the only meaningful reading since the 1-dimensional trivial representation is always irreducible. (4) 'Locally soluble' has no Mathlib definition, so a problem-file bespoke definition (every finitely generated subgroup is soluble) is used; in an actual PR it could be moved to FormalConjecturesForMathlib, but only one output file was permitted here.
